result.summary: Across two observed 5-second cycles, the workstation task consists of translating a rigid red block linearly from the left pickup zone across a central boundary line to the right drop-off zone. Because the part has a simple cuboidal geometry, low estimated mass, and follows a repeatable straight-line trajectory without requiring tactile feedback, both transfer stages can be fully automated using either the UR5e or Franka FR3 cobot equipped with a standard two-finger parallel gripper.

steps.name: Move red block to center line

reasons.text: The rigid square block translates along a straight, unobstructed path from the left zone toward the center dividing line, suitable for a two-finger parallel gripper.
Top-down perspective confirms the block maintains a constant orientation and repeatable start position with no complex manipulation required.

verifier.note: The step boundaries and linear motion to the center line match across cam0, cam1, and cam2 after accounting for each camera's offset.

steps.name: Transfer red block to right zone

reasons.text: The block crosses the center boundary line and continues along a linear trajectory to the right placement zone well within the 850 mm cobot reach.
Third camera view verifies smooth, unobstructed linear travel to a consistent end position without requiring tactile judgement.

verifier.note: The crossing of the center line at 2.0 s and 7.0 s and completion at 5.0 s and 10.0 s match what is seen in cam0, cam1, and cam2.

robot.why: Needed payload 1.15 kg: the heaviest of the parts in the automatable steps is red block at about 150 g plus a 1 kg allowance for the gripper and fingers, assuming the rated payload is at the tool flange and excludes the gripper. Every arm in the catalogue carries it; UR5e + Robotiq 2F-85 is preferred for its 5 kg payload, leaving 3.85 kg of margin (also enough: Franka FR3 (3 kg)).
